description: This is a false-colour infrared satellite image, captured by the Spot 5 sensor at 2.5 metre spatial resolution, using a 1/2/3 band combination. The image depicts a rural landscape within Europe, distributed by CNES and Airbus DS/Spot Image (© 2012). The scene primarily features extensive agricultural fields, a meandering river, and a distinct linear transport infrastructure. Land cover patterns are differentiated by colour: numerous rectangular and irregularly shaped fields show a mix of vivid red and muted greenish-beige tones. The red areas indicate strong reflectance in the near-infrared spectrum, characteristic of healthy, vigorous vegetation such as active cropland or dense grasslands. The greenish-beige areas suggest bare soil, senescent vegetation, or different crop types and growth stages. A prominent, dark blue/black linear feature runs horizontally across the image, representing a road or highway. A winding, dark blue/black river meanders through the upper and central parts of the image, bordered by intensely red vegetation, which suggests hydrophilous tall herbs or semi-natural mesophilic grasslands common in riparian zones, similar to examples found in Natura 2000 (N2K) sites. A large, irregularly shaped area of dense red vegetation is situated within a river bend in the central left, indicative of a lush vegetated area, possibly a wetland or specific grassland type within a flood plain. The image illustrates the complex spatial arrangement of agricultural Land Use / Land Cover (LULC), natural riverine ecosystems, and human infrastructure.
